(Note) 知覚する: To know or recognize something through the ears or eyes.
default.q.test-15-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) ステレオタイプの意味について意見を交わす。
In the class, the teacher prompts the students about the concept of stereotypes (ステレオタイプ), and they enthusiastically express and exchange their views and real-life impressions about what stereotypes mean.
default.q.test-15-q1-1.explanation: The grammar structure 「V-る / Nの + ことで」 expresses the method or means of carrying out an action. Used with a dictionary-form verb or a noun followed by の, it means "through doing..." or "by means of...", often describing how people gain awareness or achieve a result. The key evidence is the teacher's opening question, 「ステレオタイプの説明ができる人は？」, together with the conclusion: 「生徒たちは、「メディアの中の現実」と「自分たちが住む現実」とを比べることで、メディアが映し出す世界を、新たに認識し直す作業をしているのだ。」 This means: "By comparing 'reality in the media' with 'the reality in which they live,' the students are re-examining and developing a new understanding of the world portrayed by the media." To distinguish it from the tempting choice (d), note that although the students question advertisements about happy families or boys' toys with 「でも、それって変じゃない？」, these are concrete examples used to clarify the concept of stereotypes. The overall goal of the lesson is to discuss the meaning of stereotypes.
default.q.test-15-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The passage mentions advertising only as a means of identifying bias; it does not discuss the standards or essential elements of a good advertisement.
default.q.test-15-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) The lesson does not mention analyzing or discussing the positive and negative aspects of the media.
default.q.test-15-q1-1.why.2: ✓ (c) The students eagerly raise their hands to answer the teacher’s question about the definition of prejudice and repeatedly share diverse perspectives on its meaning.
default.q.test-15-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) The questions about advertisements are merely examples raised by the students during the discussion, not the main objective of the entire lesson.
default.q.test-23-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 4つ
Alain is 23 and is free in the afternoons and on both weekend days, fully meeting the requirement of working at least three days a week and therefore being eligible to apply for all four positions.
default.q.test-23-q1-1.explanation: The grammar pattern 「number + 以上」 is placed directly after a quantity or number and means "from this number upward," including the stated number. It is commonly used to express minimum requirements in recruitment notices, as in 「【資格】 18歳以上の男女」 (Qualifications: men and women aged 18 or older) and 「＊レジ、パン屋、クリーニングスタッフは1週間に3日以上アルバイトできる方を募集しています。」 (We are recruiting people who can work part-time at least 3 days a week as cashiers, bakery staff, or dry-cleaning staff). According to 「留学生のアランさん（23歳）は...」, Alain, a 23-year-old international student, meets the age requirement. Regarding his schedule, Alain has all day Saturday and Sunday free and is available most weekday afternoons after 1 p.m. (except Wednesday and Friday, when his classes end at 4 p.m.). He therefore fully meets the requirement expressed by 「授業がないときにアルバイトをしようと思っています」 (I plan to work part-time when I do not have classes), using the pattern 「V-ない + ときに」 (when not doing something). An important strategy for this type of reading-comprehension information question is not to count only the two full days he has free on the weekend. Alain can also work on weekday afternoons and therefore meet the requirement of working at least 3 days a week for all four jobs.
default.q.test-23-q1-1.why.0: ✓ (a) Alain meets both requirements: he is old enough (23 years old ≥ 18) and has sufficient free time (he can work more than 3 days per week), so he is eligible to apply for all four positions.
default.q.test-23-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) The option stating three jobs is inaccurate because the supermarket does not impose any condition limiting Alain to applying for only three positions.
default.q.test-23-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) Option 2, “two jobs,” is incorrect because Alain has more than two days of free time and can easily work more than two types of jobs.
default.q.test-23-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) Choice 1 is incorrect because Alain is not restricted to choosing only one job.
default.q.test-31-q3-3.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) Many people are good at foreign languages but poor at their native language.
The author clarifies the true meaning of the underlined sentence in the following sentence, pointing out that many people speak foreign languages fluently but hesitate and struggle in their native language.
default.q.test-31-q3-3.explanation: In the supporting sentence, the grammar pattern 「～のに」 (used with the plain form, with a na-adjective retaining 「な」) expresses an unexpected or paradoxical contrast between the two descriptions 「ぺらぺら」 (fluent) and 「たどたどしい」 (hesitant and halting). The direct basis for interpreting sentence ③ is the following sentence: 「外国語はぺらぺらなのに、日本語のほうはなんともたどたどしいという若者も多い。」 It means: "There are also many young people who speak foreign languages fluently, yet speak Japanese extremely haltingly." Through this sentence, the author points out that learning foreign languages is connected to the issue of one's native language: many people speak foreign languages well but have poor native-language ability. A common trap is (a), because the previous sentence mentions mastering Japanese before learning a foreign language. However, when a general observation is presented with the sentence-ending 「～のだ」, the core evidence and explanation are usually found in the immediately following sentence.
default.q.test-31-q3-3.why.0: ✗ (a) This is the viewpoint expressed in the preceding sentence about mastering one’s native language before beginning a foreign language, not an explanation of sentence ③.
default.q.test-31-q3-3.why.1: ✗ (b) The passage does not compare the difficulty of one’s native language and a foreign language or claim that they are equally difficult.
default.q.test-31-q3-3.why.2: ✓ (c) The following sentence directly explains that many young people speak foreign languages very fluently (上手), but speak Japanese hesitantly and awkwardly (下手).
default.q.test-31-q3-3.why.3: ✗ (d) The passage does not present a causal relationship or rule that improving one’s foreign-language skills automatically improves one’s native language.
default.q.test-32-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 日本語の特殊性についてのさまざまな意見や考え方
The demonstrative 「そこ」connects the context by referring back to the various rumors and hypotheses about the special characteristics of Japanese, providing a starting point for the following discussion.
default.q.test-32-q1-1.explanation: The demonstrative 「そこ」 in the connective phrase 「そこから」 uses contextual reference (文脈指示), pointing back to the events just mentioned as the starting point or cause of the following claim. The preceding context is: 「これまでにいろいろと日本語の特殊性がささやかれてきた。はては、だから日本人は外国語が苦手なのだといったもっともらしい説もとびだす。」 The author is listing various rumors and seemingly plausible theories about the distinctive nature of Japanese. The underlined sentence means: “From there, the argument developed into the claim that the number of foreigners becoming proficient in Japanese never increases (unlike in English) because Japanese is a distinctive and difficult language.” Choices (b) and (c) are traps that change the level of certainty: they turn rumors 「ささやかれてきた」 and seemingly plausible theories 「もっともらしい説」 into facts (事実) or objective observations (客観的な観察). In N2 reading comprehension, carefully check how reliable the information is. Here, 「そこ」refers to the collection of different opinions and views about the distinctive nature of Japanese, as stated in choice (d).
default.q.test-32-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The state of Japanese being isolated from the world’s languages appears at the very beginning of the passage, too far away and not a direct basis for the inference in sentence ①.
default.q.test-32-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) The passage presents Japanese people's poor foreign-language ability as a “plausible theory” (もっともらしい説), not as a “fact” (事実).
default.q.test-32-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) The points mentioned in the preceding sentence are only rumors (ささやかれてきた) and subjective hypotheses, not “objective observations” (客観的な観察).
default.q.test-32-q1-1.why.3: ✓ (d) 「そこ」 directly replaces the collection of rumors and different views about the uniqueness of Japanese mentioned immediately beforehand.
default.q.test-33-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 二酸化炭素
In the passage, carbon dioxide (二酸化炭素) is mentioned only as a greenhouse gas that water must absorb to purify the atmosphere, not as a material necessary for creating organic beings (有機体).
default.q.test-33-q1-1.explanation: The key pattern 「～を主体とした」 (N1 + を主体とした + N2) means “centered on N1” or “with N1 as the main component,” and is often used in explanatory or academic writing to identify the principal constituent of something. In paragraph 3, the author identifies carbon and oxygen as materials that make life possible: 「まず、生命を作る材料である炭素や酸素などの重元素の固まりが、岩石成分となって表面に剥き出しになっている必要があります」 ("First, masses of heavy elements such as carbon and oxygen, which are materials that make life, must be exposed on the surface as rock components.") Organic life is defined as 「炭素を主体とした化合物である有機体」 ("an organic entity that is a compound centered on carbon"). By contrast, CO2 appears only in the final sentence: 「このように、水は、エアコン作用によって惑星表面が高温にならないよう調節するとともに、「温室効果ガス」である二酸化炭素を吸収して、大気を浄化するように働いています」 ("Thus, water regulates the planet’s surface so that it does not become too hot through its air-conditioning effect, while also absorbing carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, and working to purify the atmosphere.") This shows that CO2 is merely a gas absorbed for purification, not a substance used to create organic life. Choice (c), hydrogen (水素), is tempting because the passage mentions that planets containing large amounts of hydrogen gas have no organic life. However, hydrogen combines with oxygen to form water, which the author emphasizes is indispensable (不可欠) for dissolving elements and enabling the chemical reactions that form organic compounds.
default.q.test-33-q1-1.why.0: ✓ (a) 二酸化炭素 serves only as a greenhouse gas absorbed by water to help purify the atmosphere; it is not a substance that forms organic organisms.
default.q.test-33-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) The passage explicitly states that 炭素 is a heavy element that serves as raw material for life and is a core component of organic compounds.
default.q.test-33-q1-1.why.2: ✗ (c) Hydrogen combines with oxygen to form water, an element the passage states is indispensable for promoting the reaction that produces a new compound.
default.q.test-33-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) The passage directly states that 酸素 is one of the heavy elements that serve as materials for creating life.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) こどもを保育所に預ける際にそのことが問題になるということ
Both passages A and B directly discuss how the stereotype 「三歳児神話」 makes placing children in daycare (保育所) difficult and creates significant pressure for parents.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.explanation: The central point is that both authors connect this hypothesis with placing a child in daycare. Passage A criticizes social pressure through the sentence 「母親が子どもを保育所に預けようとすると、「三歳までは母親が自分で育てないと、子どもがまっすぐに育たない」とまわりから非難されてしまうのです」, while passage B reflects parents' inner conflict through 「この神話を突きつけられた親たちは「それなら保育所で育てられた子供はみんな悪くなるのか」と反論したくなる」. The complete translations are: "When a mother tries to place her child in daycare, people around her criticize her, saying that unless a mother raises her child herself until age three, the child will not grow up properly" (passage A), and "Parents confronted with this myth want to argue, 'Then does that mean every child raised in daycare will turn out badly?'" (passage B). Grammatically, option (c) uses the N2 pattern 「〜際に」, which combines with a dictionary-form or past-form verb, or with a noun + の. It has a formal, stiff nuance equivalent to とき and indicates the time or circumstance of an action, here "when placing a child in daycare." In A-B comparison questions, beware of one-sided distractors: although options (a) and (b) contain wording that appears verbatim in the passages, each appears in only one passage. The shared keyword 保育所 (daycare) is what leads to the correct answer.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.why.0: ✗ (a) The criticism from people around them toward the parents appears only in Passage A (まわりから非難されてしまう), not in Passage B.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.why.1: ✗ (b) The idea that ordinary people find it difficult to reject content lacking scientific evidence appears only in passage B; passage A does not mention it.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.why.2: ✓ (c) Both passages clearly state that placing a child in a daycare center (保育所) creates difficulties and psychological pressure for the parents.
default.q.test-34-q1-1.why.3: ✗ (d) Passage B only expresses a general desire for countermeasures and does not propose any specific method, while Passage A does not mention it at all.
default.q.test-36-q2-2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 自分の参加した講座で使用している教科書は受付に行けば見せてもらえる。
According to the notice, participants may go to the reception desk and ask to see the textbook used in the course they attended.
default.q.test-36-q2-2.explanation: The key pattern is 「V-て + もらえる」, the potential form of 「〜てもらう」, combined with the te-form of a transitive verb. It describes receiving a favor or helpful service from another person. Here, 「見せてもらえる」means "be allowed to see" or "have someone show you something." The sentence means: "If you go to the reception desk, the staff will let you see the textbook used in the course you are taking." For comparison: 「受付で頼めば、詳細な案内図を見せてもらえます。」(If you ask at the reception desk, they will show you a detailed guide map.) In N2 information-search reading questions, choices (b) and (c) may be tempting because of traps involving seasons and levels. Compare every condition precisely instead of relying on isolated keywords.
default.q.test-36-q2-2.why.0: ✗ (a) This is incorrect because trial lectures are not freely available to everyone who wishes to take next year's spring course.
default.q.test-36-q2-2.why.1: ✗ (b) Incorrect because the lower-intermediate level does not meet the prerequisites for entering the intermediate course directly in the fall.
default.q.test-36-q2-2.why.2: ✗ (c) This is incorrect because the rules do not allow a student to enroll in both the beginner and lower-intermediate courses simultaneously starting in spring.
default.q.test-36-q2-2.why.3: ✓ (d) It is entirely possible for seminar participants to go to the reception desk to look at the materials and textbooks used in their course.
default.q.test-44-q2-2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 2円
According to the husband’s calculation, picking up a 1-yen coin consumes energy equivalent to 3 yen, resulting in a net loss of 2 yen.
default.q.test-44-q2-2.explanation: The key term 「赤字」means a deficit or loss, describing a situation in which expenses exceed returns. The sentence uses 「N＋に換算すれば」(if converted into monetary terms) and the conjectural ending 「～であろう」(would probably be ...), estimating an intangible quantity in terms of money. The relevant passage is: 「金額に換算すれば、三円位になったであろう。二円の赤字である。」 This means: “If converted into monetary terms, the amount would probably have been about three yen. That represents a two-yen deficit.” The husband recovered his one-yen coin, but thinking in the restroom consumed energy worth about three yen. To distinguish choice (d), 3円, remember that the actual loss is the energy cost minus the recovered value: 3 yen − 1 yen = 2 yen.
default.q.test-44-q2-2.why.0: ✗ (a) This is incorrect because the passage does not conclude that the loss was zero; the husband expended more energy than the value of the coin he found.
default.q.test-44-q2-2.why.1: ✗ (b) Incorrect because 1 yen is the denomination of the dropped coin, not the deficit remaining after accounting for energy loss.
default.q.test-44-q2-2.why.2: ✓ (c) Correct: the energy used is equivalent to 3 yen, and after subtracting the 1 yen that was picked up, the actual loss is 2 yen.
default.q.test-44-q2-2.why.3: ✗ (d) The 3 yen refers to the total energy consumed converted into monetary value, without yet subtracting the 1 yen recovered from what was picked up.
default.q.test-47-q2-2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 12月18日に窓口で申し込み、2,100円を支払う。
Yuki is taking the third session (第3回), so registration must be completed on December 18. As a new resident of Midori City and a first-time visitor to the center, Yuki must apply at the counter and pay the discounted resident fee of 2,100 yen.
default.q.test-47-q2-2.explanation: The passage opens with an encouraging quotation: 「一見難しそうに見えるラテ・アートですが、小学生にも挑戦できます！」, fully translated as: "Latte art may look difficult at first glance, but even elementary school students can try it!" The key grammar point is 「一見」 (at first glance) combined with an -い adjective with い removed and 「～そうに見える」 (to look/seem...), describing an initial judgment based on appearance. It often comes before the contrastive conjunction 「ですが」 to emphasize that something is not as difficult as it seems. In addition, 「気の利いた」 in 「近ごろカフェにいくと気の利いたラテ・アートをしてコーヒーを出してくれるお店が増えましたよね」 is an idiomatic expression placed before a noun, conveying a refined, skillful, and customer-oriented quality. For JLPT N2 reading-comprehension information-search questions, carefully compare the conditions for each session: Yuki is attending the third session (第3回), so he must register in December rather than October. Since he has just moved to Midori City, he is a local resident and pays 2,100円 instead of the 2,600円 nonresident fee. Also watch for the common contact-method trap: 「初めて訪問」 (visiting for the first time) means that telephone options (電話) must be eliminated because the initial procedure always requires applying in person at the counter (窓口).
default.q.test-47-q2-2.why.0: ✓ (a) This choice is correct because the registration date for the third session is 12/18, first-time visitors must register in person at the counter, and Yuki is a resident of Midori City, making her eligible for the 2,100-yen fee.
default.q.test-47-q2-2.why.1: ✗ (b) This choice is incorrect because October 17 is the registration deadline for the first round, not the third, and the fee of 2,600 yen is for people from outside the city.
default.q.test-47-q2-2.why.2: ✗ (c) This choice is incorrect because the rules clearly state that first-time visitors to the center must complete the procedure in person at the counter and may not register by phone.
default.q.test-47-q2-2.why.3: ✗ (d) This choice is incorrect in terms of the registration date (10/17 belongs to the first period), the registration method (telephone registration is not available to first-time visitors), and the fee (2,600 yen applies to people from outside the city).
default.q.test-53-q3-3.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 日本のような清潔すぎる環境では、人間の免疫システムがうまく働かなくて起きるもの
The fundamental cause is that an excessively clean living environment gives the immune system no proper target to fight, causing it to mistake pollen for an enemy and activate its protective function incorrectly.
default.q.test-53-q3-3.explanation: The key sentence is: 「スギの花粉が入ってくると、人間の免疫システムが誤って作動し、吸血ダニ退治の物質を出す。そのせいで、目がしょぼしょぼしたり、くしゃみをしたりすることになるわけです。」 (When cedar pollen enters the body, the human immune system operates incorrectly and releases substances that kill blood-sucking mites. As a result, people's eyes become irritated and they sneeze.) The pattern V-stem / adjective stem + すぎる expresses an excessive degree beyond the normal limit, usually with a negative nuance; here, 清潔になりすぎる means "become too clean." This combines with 誤って作動する, where the adverb 誤って modifies 作動する, meaning "to operate mistakenly." It describes a defense mechanism being activated incorrectly, corresponding to option (d)'s うまく働かない. Hay fever occurs because, in an excessively clean environment, the immune system has no mites to fight and its ability is wasted (宝の持ち腐れ). It therefore mistakes harmless pollen for an enemy (敵と見誤って) and attacks the wrong target. To avoid the distractor (b), distinguish between the immune system becoming weakened (弱る) and operating incorrectly (誤って作動する): the passage says that the immune system still releases powerful substances; it simply targets the wrong object.
